edges.reason: msg.sender is assigned to owner in the Owned constructor, granting full contract privilege to the deployer/caller.
transferOwnership is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier which requires msg.sender == owner.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner before ownership is moved.
approve/approveAndCall write allowed[msg.sender][spender].
transfer reads and writes balances[msg.sender] through safeSub/safeAdd.
transferFrom uses msg.sender as the spender key in allowed[from][msg.sender].
msg.sender is written into allowed and is then forwarded into the external receiveApproval callback.
transfer credits balances[to] with safeAdd.
transfer.tokens is the debited/credited amount applied to balances.
approve stores the granted amount at allowed[msg.sender][spender].
approve.tokens is written directly into the allowed mapping without checks.
transferFrom debits balances[from] using safeSub.
transferFrom credits balances[to] using safeAdd.
transferFrom.tokens is the amount moved between balances entries.
transferFrom.tokens is subtracted from allowed[from][msg.sender].
approveAndCall.spender is the target address cast to ApproveAndCallFallBack and called.
approveAndCall.tokens is passed as an argument to the external receiveApproval call.
approveAndCall.data is attacker-controlled calldata forwarded verbatim to the external call.
tokenAddress is cast to ERC20Interface and invoked without any whitelist or code check.
tokens is the amount passed to the external token transfer.
approveAndCall always executes the external receiveApproval call after writing the allowance.
The spender contract can re-enter approveAndCall during receiveApproval and rewrite allowed[msg.sender][spender].
A re-entrant spender can call transferFrom to spend the freshly granted allowance before approveAndCall returns.
The external callback can mutate the allowed mapping while the original call has already updated it.
transferAnyERC20Token is the only path that triggers the arbitrary external token transfer.
The rescued tokens are always sent to the owner address by the external transfer call.
transferOwnership stores the caller-supplied _newOwner into newOwner, the gate for later privilege transfer.
balanceOf reads balances[tokenOwner].
allowance reads allowed[tokenOwner][spender].
allowance.spender is the second index of the allowed mapping lookup.
safeAdd.a feeds a + b, the addition whose overflow is guarded by require(c >= a).
safeAdd.b feeds a + b, the addition whose overflow is guarded by require(c >= a).
safeSub.a feeds a - b, guarded by require(b <= a).
safeSub.b feeds a - b, guarded by require(b <= a).
safeMul.a feeds a * b, the multiplication whose overflow is guarded by require(a == 0 || c / a == b).
safeMul.b feeds a * b, the multiplication whose overflow is guarded by require(a == 0 || c / a == b).
safeDiv.a feeds a / b, guarded by require(b > 0).
safeDiv.b feeds a / b, guarded by require(b > 0).
safeAdd is applied to balances entries in transfer and transferFrom.
safeSub is applied to balances and allowance entries in transfer/transferFrom.
approveAndCall mutates the allowed mapping before performing the external callback.
totalSupply returns _totalSupply minus the zero-address balance.
The constructor mints the whole supply into _totalSupply.
The constructor assigns the full supply balance to the fixed deployer address.
The constructor initialises the symbol state variable.
The constructor initialises the name state variable.
The constructor initialises the decimals state variable.
balanceOf reads the balances mapping.
allowance reads the allowed mapping.
totalSupply reads balances[address(0)] when computing the circulating supply.
Local c stores a + b in safeAdd and is validated against a to detect overflow.
Local c stores the guarded subtraction result in safeSub.
Local c stores a * b in safeMul and is divided back by a to detect overflow.
Local c stores the guarded division result in safeDiv.
